subject: Joint model: shared fixed effect with categorical covariate

messages.author: 78f18e5a32647f45
messages.subject: Joint model: shared fixed effect with categorical covariate
parts:
Dear INLA community

I read in the book of Virgilio and this post that we can define a shared fixed effect using f(). The covariate used in these examples is a continuous variable. Is it possible to use a shared fixed effect for a categorical covariate in a two-likelihood joint model? I have a categorical covariate with 3 levels for both likelihoods. 

Kind regards,
Yessika

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: Joint model: shared fixed effect with categorical covariate
parts:
Hi Yessika,
You can do the same for a categorical covariate, except that you have a fixed effect for each level vs. the reference level, so you have to do it for each effect separately. Alternatively, it is possible to share a linear combination of fixed and/or random effects but that is done differently, I can provide more details if that sounds interesting to you.
Best,
Denis Rustand

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: Joint model: shared fixed effect with categorical covariate
parts:
The first technique is just an adaptation of Haavard's example that you provided in the link of your first message for a continuous covariate. The second consists in adding a third likelihood that will correspond to the shared part between the two initial likelihoods. I made an example based on Haavard's code (see attached). In the context of a categorical covariate with 3 levels, you have the fixed effect of level 2 vs. level 1 (reference) and level 3 vs. level 1., i.e.:
eta1 =... + beta1*x1 + beta2*x2 + ...
eta2 = ...+ alpha1*(beta1*x1) + alpha2*(beta2*x2) + ...

Second option is doing:
eta1 =... + beta1*x1 + beta2*x2 + ...
eta2 = ...+ alpha*(beta1*x1+beta2*x2) + ...

Best,
Denis Rustand
